approved: Sugar Research and Development Services Bill 2013

Moved the second reading of the companion Sugar Research and Development Services (Consequential Amendments and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2013, which transfers 75 per cent of the Sugar Research and Development Corporation's assets to the new industry body on its declaration and winds up the corporation by 30 September 2013, with the levy increase taking effect from 1 July 2013.

Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills as a reform backed by most of the industry, under which Sugar Research Australia would replace separate research bodies and receive a 70c per tonne levy paid equally by growers and mills, while raising concerns about consultation, regional research, conflicts of interest and the legislation's rushed 1 July 2013 commencement.

Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills and the creation of Sugar Research Australia, funded by a 70c per tonne levy, while urging the government and new board to retain research talent and address concerns about consultation, miller contributions, diversification and the closure of the Bundaberg research facility.

Supported the Sugar Research and Development Services bills, saying they would consolidate research functions in Sugar Research Australia, reduce duplication and secure funding through a 70c per tonne levy, while urging swift passage to provide certainty for research staff and the industry's future.
